summary: Integration lines delivered: playwright.config.ts (webServer `pnpm dev`, fixed test ports 5390/3390, a per-run temp DATABASE_URL and HOME/USERPROFILE, projects fresh-db -> main), tests/e2e/global-setup.ts, tests/e2e/support/fixtures.ts (outside-network blocker, native-dialog guard, API seeding with the G1-G4 cases, 390 px / axe / forbidden-term helpers), 12 e2e specs with 52 tests, and .aioson/plans/diagnostico-maturidade/harness-contract.json. Running the combined units end to end exposed five real defects that no unit pipeline could see; all were repaired at their owning paths. Final state: pnpm test 757/757, pnpm test:e2e 52/52 (three consecutive full runs), pnpm build, the three smokes and aioson harness:check 6/6.

findings.summary: `pnpm dev` (what the Play runs in dev-link) never started the backend. `tsx watch server/main.ts` hangs silently when its stdin is a pipe nobody writes to, which is what `concurrently` gives each child. Reproduced: tsx watch with stdin 'pipe' printed nothing in 12 s, with stdin 'ignore' it listened. The first e2e run timed out after 180 s waiting for /api/health (ECONNREFUSED on BACKEND_PORT).
findings.resolution: The `dev` script now runs the API with `tsx server/main.ts`, the same runner as `start`, which smoke-boot already proves. `node --watch --import tsx` was tried first and rejected: on this Windows host (NTFS last-access updates on, fsutil DisableLastAccess=2) it restarted the API on file reads, node_modules included, and dropped in-flight requests mid-test. Trade-off: the backend no longer restarts by itself on server-file edits in dev; Vite HMR for the UI is unchanged.

findings.summary: In dev the page reloaded itself about 1 s after opening whenever any file in the project folder changed (AIOSON context/runtime files, logs, test output). Tailwind's automatic source detection scanned the whole folder (it is not a git repository, so .gitignore is not applied), and @tailwindcss/vite sends `full-reload` when a scanned file that is not a module changes. Reproduced as a lost wizard submit (firstRun) and as 'Execution context was destroyed' during the keyboard checks. In the Play dev-link AIOSON writes .aioson files constantly, so the user's screen would reload at random. Words from the AIOSON docs were also compiled into CSS classes.
findings.resolution: `@import "tailwindcss" source(none);` plus `@source "../";` so only src/ is scanned. Production CSS went from 75.4 KB to 70.8 KB; every e2e and axe check passes with the change.

findings.summary: AC-dm-46: at 390 px the questionnaire scrolled horizontally (by 675 to 773 px). Below lg the page grid had an auto column that grew to the block rail's nowrap width, and the rail's sr-only '(respondido)' spans (position absolute, no positioned ancestor) escaped the rail's own overflow scroller.
findings.resolution: `grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)]` below lg on the questionnaire grid and `relative` on the rail links, so the rail scrolls inside itself.

findings.summary: AC-dm-46 contrast (axe, 4.5:1): dark --text-muted was 4.49 on dialog surfaces; light --text-muted was 3.99 on the page ground; light --copper (warn) was 4.37 on the ground and 4.34 on its own wash (risk and 'Abaixo de 50' badges); --peril (danger badge text on danger-wash) was borderline in both themes.
findings.resolution: Dark: --text-muted #8f8674 -> #958c7a and --peril #e25d5d -> #ee7c7c. Light: --text-muted #7d7362 -> #6b6252, --copper #a55a30 -> #824421 and --peril #bf3d47 -> #9e2d37. axe is clean on every route in both themes at 390 px, including the G1 result with the high-risk badge.

findings.summary: AC-dm-46 touch targets under 44 px at 390 px: company name links in the list (about 20 px tall), the 'Empresas' breadcrumb and the archive/restore/delete link buttons on the company page (the button link variant forces min-h-0, also at max-sm), and the company breadcrumb on the questionnaire (17 px).
findings.resolution: `inline-flex min-h-(--touch) items-center` on those links, and `cn(buttonVariants({ variant: "link" }), "min-h-(--touch) max-sm:min-h-(--touch)")` for the company status links.

findings.summary: The listed per-capability forms `pnpm test:e2e -- <spec>` and `pnpm test -- <files>` run the whole suite: pnpm 11 forwards the literal `--`, so Playwright and Vitest drop the file filter. Every listed form was run and exits 0 (each is a superset of the targeted check). To run one e2e file, use `pnpm exec playwright test <file>`.

@playwright/test 1.64.1 needs Chromium build 1248, which was not on this machine. `npx playwright install chromium` was run once (browser download only; no project file changed). A clean machine needs the same step before `pnpm test:e2e`. It is a developer prerequisite and is not in postinstall, so the Play install stays light.

Manual checks this unattended session cannot run (they do not block PASS): dev-link in the Play with the badge green (CAP-dm-play-runtime); opening with no data through the Play dev-link (CAP-dm-first-run, AC-dm-01; the e2e fresh-db project covers the same route); export from the Play webview (CAP-dm-report, AC-dm-36; e2e covers the Downloads save, the PDF content, cancel and failure); the AC-dm-27 timing on an ordinary Windows computer (e2e measured under 3 s on the dev stack); AC-dm-44 from another computer on the network (smoke-boot checks that the external IPv4 addresses are refused); AC-dm-45 update through the store (smoke-migrate and smoke-store-package cover it locally); the private publication and steps 1 to 5 of Phase 4 on Windows.

AC-dm-31's recalculation notice for different rules versions cannot appear on screen, because this build ships only the v1 rules. It is covered by tests/unit/compareDiagnoses.test.ts and tests/api/historyRoutes.test.ts; the e2e asserts the notice is absent when both versions match.

Only harness-contract.json was written. `aioson harness:init` would also create progress.json, which is outside this unit's write scope. `aioson harness:check` does not need it and passed 6/6 with integrity ok (runtime feature detected through the prototype manifest).
